relationship: Changing incidence angle and the refractive-index boundary connects refraction to the critical threshold and total internal reflection, with calculation checked against the visible ray behaviour.

learnerLoop.action: Predict the threshold change, adjust incidence angle, mark the transition and complete critical-angle working.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The two media and incidence angle determine refracted and reflected rays and whether a critical angle exists.
learnerLoop.evidence: The ray diagram, regime indicator and recorded calculation expose refraction, the boundary case and total internal reflection.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Compare observation with calculation and test a different refractive index or reverse the boundary.

invariants: Angles are measured from the normal and refraction follows the same index ratio used in the calculation.
A critical angle exists only from higher to lower refractive index; total internal reflection requires exceeding it.
Guidance levels change calculation support without removing the physical threshold investigation.
safeAdaptations: Change index examples and prediction wording within the existing optical model.
Adjust working support while preserving the observe, mark and calculate sequence.
nonGoals: Do not present total internal reflection as occurring at every boundary or every angle.
Do not expand into wave interference or a full optical-instrument simulator.

critical-angle.description: Observed threshold and calculated critical angle.
critical-angle.domain: asin(n outside / n inside), when a critical angle exists.
critical-angle.source: Media indices supplied; learner marks threshold; None shows calculation, Some asks angle, All asks formula/ratio/angle.
critical-angle.output: Comparison of marked threshold and calculation.

modes.none: Predict, observe both regimes and mark; calculation supplied.
modes.all: Select the ratio formula, enter sine ratio and angle.
modes.comparison: Second medium pair, then fresh practice and free media exploration.

dependencies: Both escaping light and total internal reflection must be observed before marking.
implementation.completion: finishRound requires exploration and a marked threshold; numerical checking follows the selected working level.
limitations: Ideal planar-boundary optics; displayed power is model evidence, not a separate learner answer.
